sections.name: seedTestMatch
sections.title: Creating a test match
sections.what: Creates one upcoming match with two team names and a set of players for each team, then returns the match's identifier and always closes the connection.
sections.why: Gives match screens real rows to display during tests, and the closing step prevents leaked connections.
sections.watch_out: Rows are never removed, and the helper must never run against a production database.

summary: A test helper that writes one upcoming match with two teams and fourteen players straight into the database, and returns the match identifier.
purpose: Gives browser tests a match to show on screens that need one, without the app making up data for real users.
why: The file's own comment says the app should never fabricate data shown outside tests, so the fake data is created only for testing.
how: It opens a database connection, creates a match one day in the future with two made-up team names, adds seven players for each team with fixed roles, returns the match identifier, and closes the connection even if an error happens.
inputs: No inputs. It uses a timestamp to make names unique.
outputs: The identifier of the new match.
risks: It writes real rows into whatever database the test points to, and the rows are never removed. Running it against a non-test database would add fake matches for real users.
debug: If a test cannot find a match, check the database connection the test environment uses. If duplicates pile up, the rows are not cleaned up by design.
